issue_context.title: Edge-case race condition in WebProxy
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/ncl See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
#73803 introduced a race condition when recreating the internal `Regex` list. The issue is that we update the `IsChanged` flag before we replace the `_regexBypassList` field [here](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/4da3eae7a54a4a6abeb59df4953b6de4c65b53ea/src/libraries/System.Net.WebProxy/src/System/Net/WebProxy.cs#L128-L145). If two threads query `GetProxy` or `IsBypassed` at the same time, one may not observe changes to the bypass list and return the wrong answer. ```c# var proxy = new WebProxy("myProxy:1234"); proxy.BypassArrayList.Add("contoso"); var task1 = Task.Run(() => proxy.IsBypassed(new Uri("http://contoso"))); var task2 = Task.Run(() => proxy.IsBypassed(new Uri("http://contoso"))); if (await task1 != await task2) { Console.WriteLine("Oh no"); } ``` This is limited to cases where the user modified the bypass list via the `BypassArrayList` property, which is hopefully rare.
Author: MihaZupan
Assignees: -
Labels: `bug`, `area-System.Net`
Milestone: -

Accessing a WebProxy instance while its bypass list is being changed concurrently is already not thread safe and isn't supported.

I've not looked at the code; is the issue here more that because it's lazily initialized this can happen even without concurrent user modification of the list?
I see; yeah, that's worth fixing.
Triage: Rare reliability problem. However, it is regression against 6.0. We should try to fix it in 7.0 if the fix is low-risk.
Fixed in main (8.0) in PR #75193 and in 7.0 (RC2) in PR #75246.

review_comments:
I believe this should be using a `Volatile.Write` to prevent reordering of these writes.

Edit: I don't know that it would happen in practice, but AFAIK theoretically the [reads of `IsChanged` and `_regexBypassList`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/283e351d0406d455a035b651b3d96b0209e73450/src/libraries/System.Net.WebProxy/src/System/Net/WebProxy.cs#L150-L162) could also be reordered. It likely makes sense in this case to just make `IsChanged` a `volatile` field.

TBH, I don't think read order will be changed, since compiler should know about `_regexBypassList` will be used in `UpdateRegexList()` function, if this order somehow changes, it means `code behavior in single thread` will change too. Thoughts?

> From our code's perspective, I think it's okay to be more defensive in such cases (e.g. making the field `volatile` instead of only doing a `Volatile.Write` on it).

Well, I agree on that, so I'll do necessary changes.
